brief: Goldman's model estimates CTAs sold $16bn of global equities last week, cutting net positioning to $123bn, the 75th percentile of the past year, as shorter-term trend signals neutralized or reversed. GS expects CTAs to sell another $19.5bn of global equities this week at current price and volatility levels. GS flags CTA downside convexity could turn aggressive if key SPX futures thresholds break: 7,642 short term, 7,399 medium term, 6,902 long term. Systematics are running large longs, so a break below those thresholds combined with a volatility pop could abruptly trigger the downside scenario. Separately, the corporate buyback blackout begins this week, with roughly 40% of S&P 500 companies expected to enter blackout periods, typically tempering one of the market's most consistent sources of demand. TME notes SPX remains stuck in the middle of a months-long range, with 7,600 in futures a major level near the 100-day moving average; it says to trust the current support levels or prepare for a potential supply shock from the systematic crowd.
